title.en: Dartmouth Summer Research Project: Artificial Intelligence is formally founded
title.zhHans: 达特茅斯夏季研讨会，人工智能正式诞生

summary.en: John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Claude Shannon, and Nathaniel Rochester organized an eight-week summer workshop at Dartmouth College. McCarthy coined the term "Artificial Intelligence," and the workshop established AI as an independent scientific discipline. The event is widely called "the Constitutional Convention of AI."
summary.zhHans: John McCarthy、Marvin Minsky、Claude Shannon、Nathaniel Rochester 四人在达特茅斯学院组织了为期八周的夏季研讨会。McCarthy 首次提出"Artificial Intelligence"一词，这次会议确立了 AI 作为独立学科的地位，被称为"AI 的制宪会议"。

narrative.en: In the early 1950s, the field of "thinking machines" had no unified name—it was variously called cybernetics, automata theory, or complex information processing. John McCarthy, then a young Assistant Professor of Mathematics at Dartmouth, was frustrated by the lack of focused research. He applied to the Rockefeller Foundation for funding to bring together the leading thinkers for a summer seminar. The proposal, co-authored with Minsky, Rochester, and Shannon, stated a bold conjecture: "Every aspect of learning or any other feature of intelligence can in principle be so precisely described that a machine can be made to simulate it." The workshop ran for six to eight weeks with about 20 participants cycling through. Allen Newell and Herbert Simon demonstrated their Logic Theorist—widely considered the first AI program—which could prove mathematical theorems. Arthur Samuel presented his checkers-playing program. The term "Artificial Intelligence" was chosen for its neutrality, deliberately avoiding identification with cybernetics (which was heavily associated with Norbert Wiener) or automata theory. The workshop's legacy extends far beyond the name it coined: it laid the groundwork for AI labs at MIT, Carnegie Mellon, and Stanford, and created the intellectual network that would dominate the field for the next two decades. Perhaps most importantly, it established an optimistic, ambitious research culture that—despite subsequent "AI winters"—continues to define the field today.
narrative.zhHans: 在 1950 年代早期，"会思考的机器"这个领域没有统一的名字——它被不同地称为控制论、自动机理论或复杂信息处理。John McCarthy，当时是达特茅斯学院一位年轻的数学助理教授，对缺乏聚焦的研究感到沮丧。他向洛克菲勒基金会申请资助，将顶尖思想家聚集起来举办一个夏季研讨会。与 Minsky、Rochester 和 Shannon 共同撰写的提案提出了一个大胆的猜想："学习的每一个方面或智能的任何其他特征原则上都可以被如此精确地描述，以至于可以制造一台机器来模拟它。"研讨会持续了六到八周，约有 20 名参与者流动参加。Allen Newell 和 Herbert Simon 展示了他们的逻辑理论家——被广泛认为是第一个 AI 程序——可以证明数学定理。Arthur Samuel 展示了他的跳棋程序。"Artificial Intelligence"这个名字被选中是因为它的中性，有意避免与控制论（与 Norbert Wiener 密切相关）或自动机理论同化。研讨会的遗产远超它所创造的名字：它为 MIT、CMU 和 Stanford 的 AI 实验室奠定了基础，并创建了将主导接下来二十年该领域的知识网络。也许最重要的是，它建立了一种乐观、雄心勃勃的研究文化，尽管后来经历"AI 冬天"，至今仍在定义这个领域。

description.en: Established AI as an independent scientific discipline with a unified name, research agenda, and community. The workshop's participants and their students went on to found the major AI laboratories at MIT, CMU, and Stanford.
description.zhHans: 以统一的名称、研究议程和社区，将 AI 确立为独立学科。研讨会的参与者及其学生后来创建了 MIT、CMU 和 Stanford 的主要 AI 实验室。

description.en: Created the foundation for an open academic AI community. The workshop's interdisciplinary approach—bringing together mathematicians, psychologists, engineers, and information theorists—established a collaborative rather than siloed research culture.
description.zhHans: 为开放的学术 AI 社区奠定了基础。研讨会的跨学科方法——聚集数学家、心理学家、工程师和信息论学者——建立了合作而非孤岛式的研究文化。

text.en: The Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence was held in the summer of 1956, organized by John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Claude Shannon, and Nathaniel Rochester, establishing AI as a field.
text.zhHans: 达特茅斯人工智能夏季研究项目于 1956 年夏季举行，由 John McCarthy、Marvin Minsky、Claude Shannon 和 Nathaniel Rochester 组织，确立了 AI 作为独立领域。

text.en: The workshop unified previously scattered research under the name 'Artificial Intelligence,' creating a coherent discipline with shared problems and methods.
text.zhHans: 研讨会将此前零散的研究统一在"人工智能"这一名称下，创建了一个具有共同问题和方法的一致学科。

sources.quote: In 1956, a small group of scientists gathered for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence, which was the birth of this field of research.
Widely considered to be the founding event of artificial intelligence as a field.
AI as a distinct field was formally established in 1956 at the Dartmouth Summer Research Project.
